prompt_text:
You are an entity extractor for cybersecurity reports. Perform entity-only extraction. Do not extract relations.

GOAL
Read the supplied passage and list every explicit mention of the four allowed categories below. Do not create any other label and do not output relationships.

ALLOWED CATEGORIES

1. Vulnerability — Any directly written CVE ID. Keep the surface form exactly as it appears, including odd spacing or line-break hyphens from PDFs, but put the cleaned canonical form in normalized_id.

2. Weakness — Either:
   a) a directly written CWE ID, or
   b) a natural-language flaw description that is explicitly linked to a CWE ID inside the same nearby factual unit.
   If there is no CWE ID written nearby in the text, do not tag a generic flaw description. Never guess a CWE from background knowledge or from a known CVE-to-CWE mapping.

3. Configuration — The minimal standalone name of a specific vendor product, software component, hardware device, or a full CPE string that could plausibly be the target of a Vulnerability-affects-Configuration statement.
   Keep only independently recognizable products. Omit version numbers, patch/build strings, vendor names alone, attacker or defender utilities, scanners, proxies, services, file/script names, IP addresses, ports, and vague placeholders like “server” or “endpoint”.

4. AttackTechnique — A directly written MITRE ATT&CK technique code (Txxxx) or a technique name that can be mapped to a single T-code purely from the wording in the passage. If a name appears immediately next to its code, keep the code only and drop the name. Do not tag tactic IDs starting with TA, nor software/group/campaign IDs starting with S/G/C.

CORE SPAN AND OUTPUT RULES
- Every `text` must occur verbatim in the input. `start` is inclusive, `end` is exclusive, both 0-based, and `text` must equal input[start:end].
- Tag each distinct occurrence separately; never emit two items with identical type and identical span.
- `normalized_id` must be: canonical CVE for Vulnerability, the locally written CWE for Weakness, a verified CPE 2.3 URI for Configuration, or the T-code for AttackTechnique. Use null when no verified value applies.
- Emit entities only. Do not define, infer, or print relations.
- Check the whole document: body paragraphs, tables, bullet lists, figure captions, and identifiers split across lines.

PRODUCT MENTION FILTER — evaluate every Configuration candidate in this order, skip if it fails:

A. Standalone recognizability: The substring alone must identify a concrete product/component/device/CPE without needing the surrounding vulnerability sentence. If it only looks like a product because of context, discard it.

B. Reduce to base name and fix offsets:
- Remove instance numbers: for “MyApp 1” / “MyApp 2” keep only “MyApp” with offsets covering just that word.
- Remove deployment adjectives: for “affected MyApp”, “public-facing MyApp”, “compromised MyApp” keep only “MyApp”.
- De-pluralize: if written as “MyApps”, keep only “MyApp” and shorten `end` by 1 to drop the trailing “s”. If no singular substring exists, discard.
- Never include version, patch, or build tokens in the span.

C. Hard exclusions even near exploit language: Never tag role nouns, generic infrastructure, security tooling, or operational artifacts, even if the sentence says the flaw was exploited on them or they were used for scanning, proxying, archiving, or persistence.
Examples to reject: Web Server, host, endpoint, workstation, network, agency, server alone, EDR, scanner, proxy, archiver, multi-tool, .exe/.rar/.zip/.sh/.jsp/.ashx names, IPs, ports, service labels, lone vendor, generic placeholders.
Illustration: in “flaw in Acme Portal on public-facing host using ScannerTool” the only valid product is “Acme Portal”.

D. Suite versus base:
- Keep a long multi-word span only when that contiguous string is the official family/edition name as printed, e.g. “Acme Portal Data Center and Server” when it appears contiguously as a family label, minus any instance number.
- Shorten when the extra words are location/deployment context, e.g. “Acme Portal on Web Server” -> keep only “Acme Portal”.
- Never assemble a span from non-adjacent tokens or import qualifiers from elsewhere.

E. Normalization for products: `normalized_id` may only be a verified base vendor:product CPE 2.3 URI. Do not build a CPE by joining edition words or numbers with underscores and do not invent tokens from instance labels or plurals. Example: “Acme Portal” may map to “cpe:2.3:a:acme:portal:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*” if verified, otherwise null. If uncertain, use null.

ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLES — follow the same logic, do not copy spans:

Example 1
Input: CVE-2023-1234 in MyApp exploited via T1059.
Output:
{"entities": [{"id": "E1", "text": "CVE-2023-1234", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 0, "end": 13, "normalized_id": "CVE-2023-1234"}, {"id": "E2", "text": "MyApp", "type": "Configuration", "start": 17, "end": 22, "normalized_id": null}, {"id": "E3", "text": "T1059", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 37, "end": 42, "normalized_id": "T1059"}]}

Example 2
Input: Buffer overflow (CWE-119) in FooBar from CVE-2024-0001.
Output:
{"entities": [{"id": "E1", "text": "Buffer overflow", "type": "Weakness", "start": 0, "end": 15, "normalized_id": "CWE-119"}, {"id": "E2", "text": "CWE-119", "type": "Weakness", "start": 17, "end": 24, "normalized_id": "CWE-119"}, {"id": "E3", "text": "FooBar", "type": "Configuration", "start": 29, "end": 35, "normalized_id": null}, {"id": "E4", "text": "CVE-2024-0001", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 41, "end": 54, "normalized_id": "CVE-2024-0001"}]}

DOCUMENT TO PROCESS
<text>
{text}
</text>

RESPONSE FORMAT
Return a single JSON object and nothing else, with this shape:
{"entities": [{"id": "E1", "text": "exact substring", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 0, "end": 13, "normalized_id": "CVE-..."}]}
Each item must contain exactly these fields: "id", "text", "type", "start", "end", "normalized_id". If no entities are found, return {"entities": []}.

prompt_text:
MISSION: Isolated Mention Capture — Cyber Threat Entity Collection

Objective: Find and annotate all qualifying entity mentions that stand alone. Treat every mention as independent — do not require co-occurrence with another entity type to justify tagging.

Annotate exactly these four types, no others:

• Vulnerability — Any verbatim CVE identifier in the form CVE-YYYY-NNNN, allowing longer digit sequences. Preserve the printed surface exactly, while normalizing to the canonical upper-case CVE value.

• Weakness — Either a verbatim CWE identifier like CWE-XXX, or a plain-language defect phrase that is directly tied to a CWE identifier within the same tight factual passage. Disregard a generic defect phrase when no CWE identifier appears in that local passage. Never infer a CWE from prior knowledge and never resolve it via an outside CVE-to-CWE mapping.

• Configuration — Only the examined system that could be vulnerable or be targeted: a deployed operating system, application, firmware / OS distro, or hardware device / appliance.
  In-scope positives: a concrete real product, platform, OS, hardware unit, or software component that is installed, executes, or is attacked, plus any complete CPE string when present. A Configuration is legitimate on its own; no linkage is needed. Label it in every location — titles, headings, main text, tables, bullet lists, figure captions, footnotes — not only beside a Vulnerability.
  Hard exclusions — do not label:
  a. multi-purpose shell utilities and file-transfer / synchronization programs wielded by actors;
  b. adversary proxy / exfiltration / scanning / reconnaissance utilities and post-compromise frameworks;
  c. defensive scanning / auditing offerings and services;
  d. cloud / hosting / managed-service vendors and generic infrastructure providers;
  e. broad software categories, general-purpose tools, services, bare capability descriptions;
  f. filenames, command lines / options, scripts, IP literals, port numbers, URLs;
  g. lone version / patch / build / update strings, or imprecise placeholders.
  If a surface string acts as the technique title immediately beside its technique identifier — for instance Name (TXXXX) — retain only the T-code as AttackTechnique and block any Configuration label on the name, even when the name looks like a utility or platform.
  Span selection — minimal self-sufficient core, applied consistently:
  a. Start from the full noun phrase and reduce to the fewest token(s) that still uniquely denote the product.
  b. Obligatory removal of the leading vendor / manufacturer token when the product name alone is unique and recognizable; retain vendor+product only when the product token alone is overly generic and needs the vendor to be identifiable.
  c. Obligatory removal of trailing release detail — version numbers, patches, builds, updates, and equivalent qualifiers. A version alone is never a valid extent and a version token may never be included in the extent.
  d. Never fuse product plus trailing feature / capability / module / sub-part sequence. Keep just the head product. Do not create one extended mention from a product plus capability chain.
  e. Never label isolated incidental vendors, utilities, services, filenames, IPs, ports, bare versions / patches / builds, or generic placeholders.

• AttackTechnique — Either a verbatim ATT&CK code such as TXXXX, including dotted sub-technique forms, or a technique title that maps unambiguously from the nearby phrasing. When a title stands immediately beside its T-code, retain only the T-code occurrence. Exclude tactic TA-IDs and software / group / campaign S/G/C identifiers.

Binding output constraints:
1. Each entity `text` must appear character-for-character in the source.
2. `start` and `end` are zero-based offsets with `end` exclusive, such that source[start:end] yields `text` verbatim.
3. Record every distinct occurrence at its own position, including repeats in headings, narrative, tables and lists. Do not merge duplicates from separate spans, do not skip title / header hits, and do not output the same type twice on the identical span.
4. `normalized_id` must be the canonical CVE, the CWE shown locally, a verified CPE 2.3 URI, or the ATT&CK T-code; otherwise null. For Configuration, employ only a verified canonical CPE 2.3 URI — when part/vendor/product is uncertain use null. Never synthesize a CPE by lowercasing, joining, or underscoring display words.
5. Output entities only. Do not derive, hallucinate, or print relations.
6. Each entity entry must hold exactly `id`, `text`, `type`, `start`, `end`, `normalized_id`, and the root object must contain the sole key `entities`.

Illustrative instances:
<example>
<text>
Attackers exploited CVE-2021-44228 in the Log4j component to gain initial access by exploiting a public-facing application (T1190).
</text>
<entities>
[
  {"id": "E1", "text": "CVE-2021-44228", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 20, "end": 34, "normalized_id": "CVE-2021-44228"},
  {"id": "E2", "text": "Log4j", "type": "Configuration", "start": 42, "end": 47, "normalized_id": "cpe:2.3:a:apache:log4j:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*"},
  {"id": "E3", "text": "T1190", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 124, "end": 129, "normalized_id": "T1190"}
]
</entities>
</example>

<example>
<text>
CVE-2021-26855 is a server-side request forgery (CWE-918) vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange Server.
</text>
<entities>
[
  {"id": "E1", "text": "CVE-2021-26855", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 0, "end": 14, "normalized_id": "CVE-2021-26855"},
  {"id": "E2", "text": "server-side request forgery", "type": "Weakness", "start": 20, "end": 47, "normalized_id": "CWE-918"},
  {"id": "E3", "text": "CWE-918", "type": "Weakness", "start": 49, "end": 56, "normalized_id": "CWE-918"},
  {"id": "E4", "text": "Microsoft Exchange Server", "type": "Configuration", "start": 75, "end": 100, "normalized_id": "cpe:2.3:a:microsoft:exchange_server:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*"}
]
</entities>
</example>

<example>
<text>
Used DataSync tool and NetScan scanner against VaultServer.
</text>
<entities>
[
  {"id": "E1", "text": "VaultServer", "type": "Configuration", "start": 47, "end": 58, "normalized_id": null}
]
</entities>
</example>

<example>
<text>
Globex VaultServer 4.2.1 affected; Exploit Public-Facing Application (T1190) used.
</text>
<entities>
[
  {"id": "E1", "text": "VaultServer", "type": "Configuration", "start": 7, "end": 18, "normalized_id": null},
  {"id": "E2", "text": "T1190", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 70, "end": 75, "normalized_id": "T1190"}
]
</entities>
</example>

Document for analysis:
<text>
{text}
</text>

Procedure: Inspect the entire input including narrative, tables, lists, captions, and identifiers broken over lines. Enforce the type definitions rigorously, enforce the Configuration inclusion versus exclusion catalog and the shortening directives evenly for full coverage, confirm every extent against the source prior to emission, and withhold Configuration where the candidate is tooling / scanner / provider / generic family / file / command / IP / port / version or is the technique title beside its T-code.

Required result: Return solely one JSON object, in the form {"entities": [{"id": "E1", "text": "exact substring", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 0, "end": 14, "normalized_id": "CVE-..."}]}. No surrounding commentary.
